savings.reason: Read the complete original and all five full actor contexts, including the newly held EO:12823 and EO:13118. The amendments retain or enlarge certain original functions while changing government/private membership counts and deleting Agriculture from optional observers; those surviving amended commands, expressly including original agency-designation and presidential-selection mandates separated from the numerical rules, are accounted for through the 2004 final revocation. No express clause saves EO:12757 operative authority after EO:13345 section 6(a), which is unconditional. EO:13345 sections 1-5 independently establish successor foreign-affairs assignments and Board governance, not continuing authority of the revoked order. EO:13118's historical exception for EO:12757 functions is not a savings clause against the later 2004 revocation. The judicial-review limitation does not independently preserve revoked delegations, and no accrued-rights or revival lead is present in the bounded held-original/actor and OFR/eCFR searches.

research_rationale: The full frozen dossier cures the former concrete gap by holding ACTOR_TEXT:EO:12823 in full, notwithstanding the stale machine missing-list statement that its target provision was not located. Read that complete amendment and the newly held full EO:13118, alongside the unchanged original and complete EO:13028, EO:13131 and EO:13345 contexts. EO:12823 is decisive: section 1(f) replaces the original five-government-member composition with six, section 1(g) deletes Agriculture from the optional observer permission, and section 1(k) replaces the original four-private-member composition with five. The original five-government and four-private numerical rules, and the deleted Agriculture observer permission, first end December 3, 1992, under present amendment language with no delay. The complete original agency-designation and presidential-selection mandates are separately inventoried with their shared paragraph context and retained through the July 8, 2004 revocation; numerical expansion does not terminate those mandates. The mixed original observer paragraph is partitioned into exact, disjoint Commerce, Agriculture and other-agency/shared-predicate spans; the full original paragraph establishes the governing sending-and-participation predicate for each subject. This preserves surviving Commerce/other permissions through 2004 instead of marking the whole paragraph ended in 1992. Other 1992 changes add FAA authority, rename the same Board, and update references while retaining original ATDA functions, agreement duties and officer responsibilities; each affected retained command records the amendment as a later event. EO:13028 adds section-571 functions and redesignates original section 6; EO:13131 further expands Tropical Forest/Board functions and replaces the already-amended private-member provision. These are recorded without confusing later additions/replacements with the first end of the earlier original numerical membership rules. EO:13118 amends a different order, expressly excepts EO:12757 functions, and does not supply a target cessation; its actual April 1/October 1 effective scheme is read. No own-term sunset is present. Both own-term records are identical default-condition leads: payment or authorization affects particular transactions, not the duration of the general rule; conditional reporting is likewise not an ending deadline. The final independent original Council/Board office/duty and retained permission commands end under EO:13345 section 6(a) on July 8, 2004, not publication or filing. Thus the latest original-command first end and whole-order end are July 8, 2004. New successor delegations have independent EO:13345 authority, and no savings continue this order. Complete original identity, source/text hashes and original text are unchanged; original metadata remains acceptable_as_original true and requires_page_check false, so original_pages_confirmed stays false. No conflicts are enumerated. OFR catalog/held-operative-text and cutoff eCFR coverage are accepted as adequate bounded searches; the earlier U.S. Code release is not asserted as a current predicate. No concrete material gap remains. Independent review identified that the prior complete section 4(a)/4(d) spans conflated ended counts with surviving mandates. The corrected inventory isolates the exact original count words five and four and the following complete substantive count-independent agency-designation and presidential-selection spans. Each reason identifies its full governing original paragraph; no free-text evidence or overlapping source span is introduced. The former three-way observer split is unchanged. The 1992 and 1999 count/Board amendments are recorded for both continuing mandates, whose first end is now explicitly accounted for in 2004. Whole-order end remains July 8, 2004.
